core_meaning.short_meaning: Qur'anic title meaning “the possessor of the two horns”
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Dhul-Qarnayn (ذو القرنين, “the possessor of the two horns”) is the title by which the Qur'an refers to a righteous monarch whose story is told in Surah al-Kahf (18:83–98). The Qur'an gives a title rather than a personal name, and the historical identification of the figure is disputed among exegetes and historians. As a given name it is rare and usually commemorative.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The expression is a construct (iḍāfa) of ذو “possessor of” and القرنين “the two horns”. The Qur'an uses it as a title, not as a personal name, and does not explain the epithet. Classical explanations include two locks of hair, two horns, two eras, or rule over east and west; this record reports the disagreement without adopting a speculative identification.
